title: A happy death
hookLine: Joseph is patron of a happy death, dying with Jesus and Mary near
tomorrow: Sofia's at Doña Carmen's bedside with no words. what does she do?

lines: A SCREEN DOOR, A KETTLE, THREE NAMES.
cards: Some sounds a family knows by heart: the screen door, the kettle, a grandmother sighing three names when a glass breaks or the news is bad. Jesús, María y José. Said fast, it sounds like a reflex.
Said slowly, it's an old hope. Ask what makes a death happy, and some grandmothers will answer with those same three names.

teach.b: Here's one to tell a friend tonight: Joseph never says a word in the Gospels. He listens to dreams, gets up, and goes.

After the boy Jesus is found in the Temple, Luke says, in the Douay-Rheims Bible, "he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject to them," and after that the Gospels never show Joseph again.

teach.h: THE GOSPELS DON'T SAY HOW HE DIED.
teach.b: They don't say how he died.

teach.h: JESUS ON ONE SIDE, MARY ON THE OTHER.
teach.b: Tradition fills the silence with a scene: Joseph at the end of his life in Nazareth, Jesus on one side, Mary on the other. That picture is why Catholics call him patron of a happy death.
Happy here doesn't mean cheerful or painless.
It means dying at peace and in grace, with the sacraments and the people you love close by.

So an old prayer some families know by heart asks Jesus, Mary and Joseph to stay near in the last agony, and to let the soul go out in peace with them. Three names, said at a deathbed, and on ordinary days long before.

how: Catholics honor Joseph on his feast days and pray to him for a good death; some families keep a picture or candle of Saint Joseph, and the short prayer to Jesus, Mary and Joseph is said at deathbeds and in daily life.

o: dying at peace, in grace, with help near
dying old, after a long and full life
dying suddenly, without pain or warning

games.q: your neighbor says she hopes to die suddenly in her sleep, "the happy death, no warning." what did the old Catholic hope mean by a happy death?
o: at peace, in grace, with the sacraments and loved ones near.
quick and painless, without knowing it was coming.
late in life, after every goal had been reached.
games.why: the old hope was a death with time to be ready and with help near, the way tradition says Joseph died, Jesus and Mary beside him.

practice: Find one steady light: a candle if you can light one safely, or a lamp across the room. Rest your eyes on it. On three slow breaths, say one name each, quietly: Jesus, on the first; Mary, on the second; Joseph, on the third.
If you pray to Joseph, you can ask him for a good death, yours or someone else's, then keep watching the light.

wordCard.voice: A happy death. Not a cheerful one: a death at peace, in grace, with Jesus, Mary and Joseph near.

orig.note: Latin: a good death. the old name for the hope Catholics entrust to Joseph.

carryVoice: Carry this: Jesus, Mary, Joseph, three names for the end and for every day before it. See you tomorrow.
